rationale: C12 is a highly specific and nearly contemporaneous drafting template. Both orders concern lands acquired under the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act or Title III of the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act, recite the same 1938 transfer and 1940 amendment, find the lands suitable for national-forest purposes, and use the same operative machinery to extend a national forest's exterior boundaries and reserve qualifying federal lands as part of that forest. C01 is also materially connected because it supplies the underlying transfer framework and substantially overlapping McCurtain County land description, while C08 supplies closely related reservation language, but neither matches the child's complete structure as closely as C12.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS certain lands in the States of Georgia, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Oklahoma have been acquired by the United States under the authority of the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 ... or Title III of the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS certain lands in the State of Utah have been acquired by the United States under the authority of the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 ... or Title III of the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act
shared_material.explanation: The opening recital uses the same distinctive statutory-acquisition formulation, adapted to different states and projects.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS, by reason of the transfer effected by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of June 9, 1938, as amended by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of August 31, 1940, such projects are now being administered pursuant to Title III of the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS, by reason of the transfer effected by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of June 9, 1938, as amended by [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of August 31, 1940, such project is now being administered pursuant to Title III of the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act
shared_material.explanation: This is nearly verbatim shared language describing the same administrative history.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS it appears that such lands are suitable for national-forest purposes and that it would be in the public interest to include them in and reserve them as parts of certain hereinafter-designated national forests
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS it appears that such lands are suitable for national-forest purposes and that it would be in the public interest to include them in and reserve them as part of the Wasatch National Forest
shared_material.explanation: The suitability and public-interest recital is closely reproduced and generalized from one forest to several.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The exterior boundaries of the Chattahoochee National Forest ... the Kisatchie National Forest ... the Holly Springs National Forest ... and the Ouachita National Forest ... are hereby extended to include ... the areas hereinafter described; and ... all lands of the United States within such areas ... are hereby added to and reserved as parts of the respective national forests
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The exterior boundaries of the Wasatch National Forest are hereby extended to include the lands hereinafter described, and, subject to valid existing rights, all lands of the United States within such boundaries as thus extended ... are hereby included in and reserved as parts of the Wasatch National Forest
shared_material.explanation: The operative clause follows the same sequence and legal mechanism: boundary extension, qualification of federal lands within the extension, and reservation as national-forest lands.
